subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: What Discord active-target precedence should OpenClaw enforce when a shared channel message names or mentions another configured agent, a role, quoted text, or another bot?
rationale: The source-level bug is real, but changing preflight from broad default/binding routing to stricter target selection can suppress existing multi-agent workflows and needs an owner-approved Discord routing contract.

options.title: Adopt strict active-target gating
options.body: Drop or reroute messages before default admission when the opening attention signal clearly targets another configured agent or unrelated role, and ignore quoted/later mentions for activation.

options.title: Keep current broad routing
options.body: Leave default/binding routing permissive and document the tradeoff for multi-agent Discord rooms instead of changing message admission semantics.

options.title: Narrow to bot-loop prevention only
options.body: Handle only bot-authored reply/loop cases through the open narrower PR and keep role/plain-text/quoted targeting out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict active-target gating
recommendation.body: Drop or reroute messages before default admission when the opening attention signal clearly targets another configured agent or unrelated role, and ignore quoted/later mentions for activation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated ownership of the shared mention policy and Discord preflight path that would encode the final precedence rule.
